newsitem.title: FRANCE: New European agency suggested to protect seas.
newsitem.headline: New European agency suggested to protect seas.

text.p: Europe should consider creating a new agency to protect its seas from overfishing, pollution and other such threats, former Portuguese president Mario Soares said on Tuesday.

Soares, chairman of the Independent World Commission on the Oceans, told a news conference his suggestion aimed to "coordinate the interests of all European countries...and to promote contacts and cooperation over oceans."
Speaking at the 40-nation Council of Europe in Strasbourg, Soares said a new European agency could cooperate to manage fish stocks and also combat maritime smuggling and illegal dumping.

He was to discuss the idea with European Commission chief Jacques Santer and the head of the Council of Europe, Daniel Tarschys, during his visit to Strasbourg. The Council of Europe seeks to promote democracy and human rights.

Soares' 43-member commission, launched in 1995 to gather evidence on the state of the world's oceans, is to present its final report to the U.N. General Assembly in 1998 -- designated international year of the oceans.
